issue.title: possible issues with circular references

body:
Judging from [the test](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/3cdb5063f20887a30101fe21748a4c4583255ce3/test/parallel/test-assert.js#L384-L396), this is sort of by design. The original behavior was (apparently) to loop forever but now it throws an error instead.

Should be fixable by keeping track of seen references. Not sure about the semver implications or if the Locked status of the API is an issue here or not. (I would consider this a bugfix myself, but others may disagree.)

@Trott I’ve looked a bit at the original issue linked above, and I think Ryan Dahl actually just forgot to pull in the patch which does what you suggest (https://github.com/nodejs/node-v0.x-archive/issues/207#issuecomment-323366). Would say it’s a bugfix, too.
@addaleax Cool! I think I've got a fix almost ready to go, but if you're already working on it, I'm happy to drop it and go do something else.
@Trott No, sorry, didn’t mean to imply that I was coding anything right now – go ahead! :smile:

Thank you!
-->
- **Version**: 6
- **Platform**: OSX 10.11.4
- **Subsystem**:

<!-- Enter your issue details below this comment. -->

Node process starts using a 100% CPU core after updating from 5.10.1 to version 6. Not sure what other details to give other that I ran `npm start` on my project which runs the following command: `webpack-dev-server --port 4444 --hot --inline --progress --colors`. I have the same running at 0.0 CPU usage right now with version 5.10.1.
If you need more information, please let me know.
